project.commit_note: The exact staged vulnerable source analyzed here is the ARVO workspace checkout HEAD `24e2d2fef88e25208ddd9fdd9c8178b9924f277d`. Its `src/ncp-spinel/SpinelNCPInstance-DataPump.cpp:317`, `src/ncp-spinel/SpinelNCPInstance.cpp:2406/2507`, `src/util/IPv6Helpers.cpp:29`, and `src/wpantund/wpantund.cpp:505/516` lines match the saved AddressSanitizer stacks used below. ARVO metadata separately reports `ad932579a99bdacf54e63b52ad8bb09d99887651` as the issue's vulnerable commit, but the staged crash path is grounded in this later workspace snapshot.
project.fixed_commit_note: The staged `patch.diff` / metadata fixed commit `418ff172c11c5f99fc15af376fb6cd5c9ac14946` only adds off-mesh-route management and does not touch `MainLoop` destruction, `SpinelNCPInstance::ncp_to_driver_pump`, the `SPINEL_PROP_THREAD_ON_MESH_NETS` inserted-value branch, or `IPv6Helpers.cpp`. Local wpantund history later contains commit `322c36f345017c47816380790aa4bd6adf50415a` (`ncp-spinel: Fix for NULL dereference on malformed packet`) on the same dereference site, but Stage 01 preserved only the vulnerable ASan UAF trace and Stage 02 did not validate any fixed revision.

classification.classification_note: The saved runtime evidence is `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free READ of size 16` from freed `SpinelNCPInstance` storage. A later local commit adds a `prefix != NULL` guard at the same callsite, but Stage 02 does not treat that later null-check hardening as demonstrated remediation for the witnessed freed-buffer read.

analysis_state.reason: Stage 01 reproduced the saved AddressSanitizer crash in `in6_addr_to_string`. The exact staged source closes the first callback's `SpinelNCPInstance` allocation at `MainLoop::MainLoop()`, the ASan-grounded free at `MainLoop::~MainLoop()`, libFuzzer's same-process leak-detection re-execution at `TryDetectingAMemoryLeak()` / `ExecuteCallback()`, the second callback's fresh `MainLoop` / `NCPInstance::alloc()` constructor path, and the later parser/sink suffix `ncp_to_driver_pump -> handle_ncp_spinel_callback -> handle_ncp_spinel_value_inserted -> in6_addr_to_string`. What the staged artifacts still do not identify is the concrete project-side alias, registration, or queued callback that bypasses that fresh second allocation and re-enters the first freed `SpinelNCPInstance`. `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to `false`, so this GT keeps that bridge explicit and unresolved instead of guessing it.

bug_description.normalized: The staged 1688-byte witness begins with mode byte `'1'`, so `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` selects `NCPInputFuzzTarget()` and feeds a raw byte stream into wpantund's NCP socket. Offline decoding of that staged stream shows a later `0x7e`-delimited fragment whose header is `0x80`, command `7` (`SPINEL_CMD_PROP_VALUE_INSERTED`), and property key `0x5a` (`SPINEL_PROP_THREAD_ON_MESH_NETS`). AddressSanitizer shows the first callback allocates a `SpinelNCPInstance` through `NCPInstance::alloc()` / `MainLoop::MainLoop()` and later frees it at `MainLoop::~MainLoop()` line 516. LibFuzzer then runs `TryDetectingAMemoryLeak()` and executes the same witness again in the same process. The staged source shows that second callback again goes through `NCPInstance::alloc()` and the plugin allocator's `return new SpinelNCPInstance(settings)` path, yet the crash-side parse/log suffix still reads 16 bytes from the first freed heap region: `ncp_to_driver_pump()` reparses the frame from `mInboundFrame`, `handle_ncp_spinel_callback()` extracts `value_data_ptr`, `handle_ncp_spinel_value_inserted()` unpacks `prefix` with `spinel_datatype_unpack(..., "6CbCb", ...)`, and `in6_addr_to_string(*prefix)` passes those bytes to `inet_ntop()`. The staged artifacts therefore ground the free site, the second callback, the fresh second allocation, and the later parser-to-sink suffix, but they do not reveal the concrete project-side stale reference or callback that bridges the first freed object to the later use. The staged metadata patch `418ff172...` is unrelated to this path, and the later local `322c36f...` null-check hardening was not validated here.

source.description: First project-side statement on the later callback path that reparses attacker-controlled inbound-frame bytes and materializes the callback dispatch command from them. ASan still places those bytes inside the first callback's freed `SpinelNCPInstance` region, so the exact bridge into this use remains unresolved.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is 1688 bytes (sha256 `37a3616dd607327d690dcfd1d5454bb9e8970ac4a0ffcd3b3bebaea7349870bb`). Byte 0 is ASCII `'1'`, so the harness selects `NCPInputFuzzTarget()`. Offline decoding of the later `0x7e`-delimited fragment 95 yields header `0x80` and command `7` (`SPINEL_CMD_PROP_VALUE_INSERTED`), which this statement extracts from `mInboundFrame` on the crash-side second callback.

sink.description: ASan sink. `inet_ntop()` reads 16 bytes through the `addr` reference previously bound from `*prefix`; on the saved run that `in6_addr` still lives inside the first callback's freed `SpinelNCPInstance` region, not the fresh object allocated for the second callback.
sink.note: The sanitizer trace reports `heap-use-after-free READ of size 16` here. The crash address `0x63100000f7c5` is 61381 bytes inside the 66832-byte region freed by `MainLoop::~MainLoop()` line 516.

root_cause.description: ASan-grounded free site. The first callback destroys its `SpinelNCPInstance`, yet the later sink still reads from that region even though libFuzzer's second callback re-runs the constructor path.
root_cause.note: The staged source shows the second callback would allocate a fresh object through `NCPInstance::alloc()`, so the missing bridge is some other project-side persistent alias or callback not exposed by the saved artifacts. With `runtime_disambiguation` disabled, Stage 02 anchors the lifetime root cause at this observed free site instead of speculating beyond the evidence.

tainted_value_origin.description: This unpack materializes the exact pointer later read at the sink. Format `6` returns `prefix` as a pointer into `value_data_ptr` rather than copying 16 bytes, so on the crash-side callback `prefix` inherits whichever `SpinelNCPInstance` storage still backs `cmd_data_ptr == mInboundFrame`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The same witness fragment's property key `0x5a` reaches this branch through `handle_ncp_spinel_callback()`. Because `value_data_ptr` still points into `cmd_data_ptr == mInboundFrame`, the returned `prefix` is another alias into that same frame storage; ASan later shows the sink read lands in the step-1 region freed at step 2 rather than the fresh object allocated at step 4.

parser_admitted.description: The crashing fragment passes the header-flag and IID-zero checks at lines 303-315, so `ncp_to_driver_pump()` admits it as a callback frame and dispatches it into `handle_ncp_spinel_callback()`.

evidence_limitations: The saved ASan stacks prove that the later `in6_addr_to_string()` read lands inside the first callback's freed `SpinelNCPInstance` region, and staged source shows the second callback would allocate a fresh object through the same constructor path, but the artifacts do not identify which other project-side alias or callback bypasses that fresh allocation and re-enters the first object.
`run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to `false`, so Stage 02 did not add marker instrumentation to resolve that stale-reference bridge.

The staged `patch.diff` / metadata fixed commit `418ff172...` is unrelated to this path. Local history later adds a same-site `prefix != NULL` guard in commit `322c36f...`, but Stage 02 did not execute or validate that revision against the witnessed UAF.

coarse_trace.summary: On the first libFuzzer callback, wpantund constructs `MainLoop` and allocates the `SpinelNCPInstance` heap region that ASan later reports as the freed allocation.
ASan's free stack shows the first callback destroying that `SpinelNCPInstance` here.

LibFuzzer immediately re-executes the same witness in the same process. The second callback also runs wpantund's constructor path again, but ASan still maps the later read to the first freed region, so the surviving project-side stale alias remains unresolved.
The crash-side callback path reparses a later inbound frame from `mInboundFrame`, extracts command `SPINEL_CMD_PROP_VALUE_INSERTED`, and dispatches it into `handle_ncp_spinel_callback()`.
The on-mesh-net branch unpacks `prefix` as a pointer into the same frame storage and passes `*prefix` into `in6_addr_to_string()`.
`inet_ntop()` reads 16 bytes from that `prefix`-derived reference, and AddressSanitizer reports that the accessed bytes belong to the region freed at step 2.

fine_trace.note: MainLoop allocates one `SpinelNCPInstance` for the NCP-input harness. ASan's allocation stack for the later crashing region is `wpantund_ncpinstance_default_alloc -> NCPInstance::alloc -> MainLoop::MainLoop`.
At the end of the first libFuzzer callback, MainLoop frees that same `SpinelNCPInstance`. ASan's free stack names this destructor and returns through `RunOneTest:273`.

LibFuzzer leak detection immediately re-executes the same witness in the same process after step 2. The saved free stack ends at `RunOneTest:273`, while the crash stack comes from `TryDetectingAMemoryLeak -> ExecuteCallback -> RunOneTest:274`, so later steps occur on this second callback.

This second callback executes the same constructor path again. `NCPInstance::alloc()` calls the plugin allocator, whose staged macro expansion returns `new SpinelNCPInstance(settings)` rather than a cached singleton. The later ASan read still lands in the step-1 region, so the missing bridge is some other surviving project-side alias or callback.

Source. On the crash-side callback, `spinel_datatype_unpack` reparses attacker-controlled frame bytes from `mInboundFrame` and materializes command `7` from the witness fragment. Because step 4 already created a fresh `SpinelNCPInstance` yet ASan later maps the read to the step-1 region, this `mInboundFrame` use must still alias the first freed object through an unresolved project-side stale reference.

Because the parsed header carries `SPINEL_HEADER_FLAG` and IID 0, this line dispatches the inbound frame into `handle_ncp_spinel_callback()`. The parser-to-callback suffix is grounded; the unresolved part is still which project-side stale reference made this call operate on step-1 storage.

The callback unpacks property `key` and `value_data_ptr/value_data_len` from `cmd_data_ptr`. For the witness fragment, `key` is `0x5a` (`SPINEL_PROP_THREAD_ON_MESH_NETS`), so the payload blob driving the crash is now materialized from bytes inside `mInboundFrame`.

The inserted-value handler selects the on-mesh-net branch because the unpacked property key is `SPINEL_PROP_THREAD_ON_MESH_NETS`. After this control decision, the function treats the blob as a `6CbCb` tuple and prepares to read the prefix from it.

This unpack does not copy the IPv6 prefix. It returns `prefix` as a pointer into `value_data_ptr`; because `value_data_ptr` itself aliases `mInboundFrame`, `prefix` now points at 16 bytes inside whichever `SpinelNCPInstance::mInboundFrame` storage still backs the callback. The sink later shows those bytes belong to the region freed at step 2, not merely to the fresh object from step 4.

fine_trace.code:
syslog(LOG_INFO, "[-NCP-]: On-mesh net added \"%s/%d\" stable:%s local:%s flags:%s", in6_addr_to_string(*prefix).c_str(),
			prefix_len,	stable ? "yes" : "no", is_local ? "yes" : "no",	on_mesh_prefix_flags_to_string(flags).c_str());
fine_trace.note: The log call dereferences `*prefix` and passes it by reference into `in6_addr_to_string()` without checking that the pointed-to storage is still live. Local history later adds only `if (prefix != NULL)` around this callsite; on the saved run `prefix` is non-null, and the later sink shows that its referenced bytes were already freed.

Sink. `inet_ntop()` reads 16 bytes from the `in6_addr` reference bound at step 10. ASan reports `heap-use-after-free READ of size 16` here, with crash address `0x63100000f7c5` located 61381 bytes inside the 66832-byte region freed at step 2.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Partially. ASan directly ties the crashing bytes to the heap region allocated through `wpantund_ncpinstance_default_alloc -> NCPInstance::alloc -> MainLoop::MainLoop` and freed at `MainLoop::~MainLoop()` line 516. The staged source also shows the second callback would allocate a fresh object at step 4, so the unresolved part is which other stale reference keeps the first region reachable.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Partially. The crash stack exactly matches steps 5-11's later callback suffix `ncp_to_driver_pump -> handle_ncp_spinel_callback -> handle_ncp_spinel_value_inserted -> in6_addr_to_string`, and libFuzzer's `RunOneTest:273` / `TryDetectingAMemoryLeak -> ExecuteCallback -> RunOneTest:274` frames match steps 2-4's first-free / second-callback sequence. The missing source-level fact is the project-side alias or callback that bridges step 2 to step 5 despite the fresh step-4 allocation.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Partially. On the observed crash-side callback path, the witness fragment becomes `command_value`, then `key/value_data_ptr`, then `prefix`, and step 10 binds `*prefix` into the `addr` reference read by `inet_ntop()`. The staged artifacts do not identify what stale reference makes that parser path run on step-1 storage after step 2.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` / metadata fixed commit `418ff172c11c5f99fc15af376fb6cd5c9ac14946` adds off-mesh-route support and does not touch the free-before-use chain reviewed here. Local history later contains commit `322c36f345017c47816380790aa4bd6adf50415a` with a same-site `prefix != NULL` guard, but that later change is not the staged patch and was not validated against the witnessed UAF.
sanitizer_ground_truth.evidence_note: The staged `reproduction_report.json`, `default_crash_trace.txt`, and `sanitizer_trace.txt` all agree on the observed AddressSanitizer `heap-use-after-free READ of size 16` in `in6_addr_to_string`. The saved ASan region report places the read address inside the heap allocation freed by `MainLoop::~MainLoop()`.

format.name: wpantund-fuzz mode-1 NCP input stream
format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are limited to the exact staged 1688-byte witness `poc` (sha256 `37a3616dd607327d690dcfd1d5454bb9e8970ac4a0ffcd3b3bebaea7349870bb`) as interpreted by `wpantund-fuzz`. Byte 0 must remain ASCII `'1'` so `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` selects `NCPInputFuzzTarget()`. The remaining bytes are consumed as the harness's raw one-byte write stream, including `0x7e` frame delimiters and any special-command handling. For this exact witness, one later `0x7e`-delimited fragment (index 95 in an offline split of the staged stream) must still decode to header `0x80`, command `7` (`SPINEL_CMD_PROP_VALUE_INSERTED`), and property key `0x5a` (`SPINEL_PROP_THREAD_ON_MESH_NETS`) so callback parsing reaches `handle_ncp_spinel_value_inserted()` and its on-mesh-net branch. The saved ASan trigger also depends on libFuzzer's leak-detection re-execution in the same process after a first pass that frees `MainLoop` / `SpinelNCPInstance`; the staged artifacts do not isolate which project-side stale reference makes the later callback run on freed object storage. This contract is limited to that exact witness and observed execution model; it does not generalize to other mode bytes, frame layouts, or property insertions.
